ThingDef.label: knucklebone mat
ThingDef.description: A pegged-out hide scattered with polished animal knuckles and a handful of wager stones. Players take turns casting the bones, calling the count, and losing tomorrow's meat ration to someone with better luck. It asks nothing of a colony's technology - only somewhere dry to sit - which makes it the one thinking game a tribe can raise on its first day.

ThingDef.label: shadow lantern theater
ThingDef.description: A stretched linen screen with a lamp behind it and a vaned drum that the flame's own heat keeps slowly turning. Painted panels ride the drum and their shadows walk across the cloth: a horse, a rider, geese going over. Nobody has to work it and nobody has to be clever at it. People drift in, sit down, and watch a procession that has been going round for hours.\n\nA whole room can watch at once. Wants a few tiles of clear floor in front of it.

ThingDef.label: pinball machine
ThingDef.description: A solenoid-and-relay amusement table: one steel ball, two flippers, and a slab of glass between the player and a playfield of bumpers that whack the ball back the moment it touches them. The scoring reels clatter loudly enough to be heard three rooms away, which is either charm or grounds for a formal complaint, depending on who you ask.\n\nRewards a steady hand and good timing - regular play trains shooting.

ThingDef.label: boomalope blitz pinball
ThingDef.description: The same cabinet, rebuilt around a herd-chase theme and a pair of chemfuel flash pots that cough a gout of harmless flame over the backglass on a jackpot. The art is a lurid green boomalope going up like a dropped lamp. Colonists who have actually watched a boomalope go up find this hilarious, horrifying, or both.\n\nThe flash pots draw extra power and make it a rowdier, more memorable table than the standard build.

ThingDef.label: mech rampage pinball
ThingDef.description: A solid-state table with a microchip scoring brain, a ramp shaped like a downed centipede, and a voice chip that barks threats in mechanoid cant. Tighter shots, harsher tilt sensor, far more satisfying to beat.\n\nThe electronics hold a running high-score table, and colonists will absolutely fight over it.

ThingDef.label: archotech dreamtable
ThingDef.description: A glitterworld pinball cabinet with no ball in it. The table reads the player's hands a half-second before they move and projects a ball that was always going to be exactly where they swing - so every player, however clumsy, walks away convinced they are extraordinary at pinball.\n\nIt is a very expensive, very beautiful lie, and nobody who plays it wants it corrected.

ThingDef.label: Ore Rush arcade table
ThingDef.description:
A sit-down arcade cabinet with the screen lying face up under a sheet of glass and a joystick at each of two seats. ORE RUSH: you are down a mine shaft with a hard hat and a lamp, clearing seams of ore one corridor at a time, and the things that live down there are coming along the same corridor from the other direction. The picture flips between turns so both seats play it the right way up.

Left alone it drops into attract mode and sits there running its title screen at nobody, which is somehow the most convincing thing about it.

Seats two - set a chair on either side. Quick reflexes help, and the ribbing that comes with them is half the point.

ThingDef.label: massage chair
ThingDef.description: A heavy reclining chair stuffed with rollers, cams and a small motor that works its way up and down the occupant's spine. It is not subtle and it is not quiet, but twenty minutes in one takes the edge off a week of hauling.\n\nColonists get in rather than sit beside it. With the power off, or switched off, nobody will use it for recreation - but it is still a chair, and a very comfortable one, so colonists will happily sit in it to eat or talk.

ThingDef.label: hologame pod
ThingDef.description: A waist-high emitter well that throws a board of light above itself and lets one player push the pieces around with their hands. It ships with a few thousand strategy games and generates more when those run out, each one tuned to sit just past the edge of the player's ability.\n\nLosing to it is good for you, apparently. It trains intellectual skill.

ThingDef.label: vista panel (1 tile)
ThingDef.description:
A wall-mounted display showing somewhere with a horizon in it. The feed runs on the local clock - grey dawn, open daylight, a long sunset, then stars - and the panel throws enough light into the room to cast the right colour of shadow at the right hour.

It is not a window and nobody is fooled for long, but a room with one in it stops feeling quite so much like a hole in the ground. Colonists in the room it faces hold off cabin fever for longer, though it will never do the job of actually going outside.

Mounts into the wall itself and takes up no floor, so shelves, chairs and anything else can stand right in front of it. It turns to face the room on its own. Needs one tile of wall.

ThingDef.label: vista panel (2 tiles)
ThingDef.description:
A wall-mounted display showing somewhere with a horizon in it. The feed runs on the local clock - grey dawn, open daylight, a long sunset, then stars - and the panel throws enough light into the room to cast the right colour of shadow at the right hour.

It is not a window and nobody is fooled for long, but a room with one in it stops feeling quite so much like a hole in the ground. Colonists in the room it faces hold off cabin fever for longer, though it will never do the job of actually going outside.

Mounts into the wall itself and takes up no floor, so shelves, chairs and anything else can stand right in front of it. It turns to face the room on its own. Needs two tiles of unbroken wall; it hangs to one side of the tile you place it on.

ThingDef.label: vista panel (3 tiles)
ThingDef.description:
A wall-mounted display showing somewhere with a horizon in it. The feed runs on the local clock - grey dawn, open daylight, a long sunset, then stars - and the panel throws enough light into the room to cast the right colour of shadow at the right hour.

It is not a window and nobody is fooled for long, but a room with one in it stops feeling quite so much like a hole in the ground. Colonists in the room it faces hold off cabin fever for longer, though it will never do the job of actually going outside.

Mounts into the wall itself and takes up no floor, so shelves, chairs and anything else can stand right in front of it. It turns to face the room on its own. Needs three tiles of unbroken wall.

ThingDef.label: dreamloop holotheater
ThingDef.description:
A bank of five emitters that fills the room in front of it with a shared waking dream - not a picture on a wall, but weather, crowds, and coastline standing in the open floor. Everyone watching gets the same dream, which is why the arguments afterwards are so specific.

A whole room can watch at once, including people lying in bed nearby. It is enormously entertaining and enormously expensive to run.

It needs a wall to throw the picture onto: face it across the room at one, up to twelve tiles away, with the audience in between. While you are placing it, the wall it will use is outlined, and if it is pointing at nothing it turns itself toward a wall that is in range. Aim it at a particular wall and it stays aimed there.

ThingDef.label: soaking tub
ThingDef.description: A deep banded barrel with a small firebox slung underneath it. Fill it, light the box, and in half an hour there is enough hot water to put a person back together after a week of hauling rock.\n\nColonists get in rather than sit beside it, and it warms the room while it burns. Runs on wood.

ThingDef.label: heated soaking tub
ThingDef.description: The same barrel with the firebox taken off and an element dropped in, so it holds temperature instead of drifting cold the moment somebody forgets to feed it. No logs, no ash, no smoke - just a standing draw on the grid whether anyone is in it or not.\n\nColonists get in rather than sit beside it, and it warms the room while it runs. It still holds only one soak, so the water is carried out by hand between uses unless it has been plumbed in.

ThingDef.label: aquarium
ThingDef.description: Two hundred litres of filtered water, a pump, a hood lamp and whatever the last trade caravan was willing to part with. The fish do nothing useful whatsoever, which appears to be the point - people stand in front of it and come away calmer than they went in.

ThingDef.label: skittles lane
ThingDef.description: Seven tiles of planed board with a shallow gutter down each side, and nine turned pins standing in a diamond at the far end. Roll the ball down, knock over what you can, then walk up and set them again - because nothing here does it for you. The old game that ten-pin bowling was eventually made from, and it eats floor space exactly the way the real thing does.\n\nThe pins stay down after about three games until somebody sets them. The thrower stands off the near end, and steady rolling trains shooting.

ThingDef.label: bowling lane
ThingDef.description: The same game with the work taken out of it. Oiled boards, ten pins in a triangle, a ball return that rolls the ball back to the player, and a pinsetter at the far end that sweeps the deck and stands the pins up between frames. Nobody walks down the lane, nobody bends over, nobody argues about whether that one was already leaning.\n\nDraws power for the machinery. Trains shooting.

ThingDef.label: karaoke machine
ThingDef.description: A screen, two speakers and a microphone on a short cord. It scrolls the words, it keeps the tune, and it is entirely indifferent to whether anyone can sing. A crowd gathers because the alternative is being the one holding the microphone.\n\nWhoever is singing enjoys themselves regardless. Everyone else in the room makes up their own mind: a colonist who can actually hold a tune wins the room over, one who cannot very much does not, friends are more forgiving than strangers, and some colonists were never going to enjoy this under any circumstances. A turn at the microphone is practice at both singing and handling a crowd, so it builds artistic and social skill together.

ThingDef.label: gravball court
ThingDef.description: A plated floor with four field emitters at the corners, holding a ball in a lazy orbit somewhere above knee height. Players work the edges and try to put it through the far ring. The gravity is a suggestion rather than a rule, and so, after a while, is the score.\n\nSeveral colonists play at once. It is properly physical, and trains melee.

ThingDef.label: armillary sphere
ThingDef.description: A nest of graduated brass rings on a tripod, with a small gilded world hanging at the centre of them. The rings are the horizon, the equator and the sun's yearly path, and turning them against each other tells you where in the sky to expect things and roughly what day it is.\n\nNo colony needs one. Colonists who stop to work out what it is saying come away calmer than they went in, which is reason enough.

ThingDef.label: tabletop orrery
ThingDef.description: A hardwood case with a geared brass model of the local system set into it, three worlds on jointed arms around a lamp-lit sun. Wind the crank and the whole thing steps forward a day at a time, the inner world hurrying, the outer one barely moving.\n\nColonists argue about whether it is accurate. It is not, particularly, but it is hypnotic.

ThingDef.label: grand orrery
ThingDef.description: A floor-standing clockwork model of the system under a glass dome, two paces across, with an engraved band of the year running round the rim. Five worlds on brass arms, one of them carrying a moon of its own, all of them creeping round a gilded sun at their proper relative speeds.\n\nIt does nothing. It costs a fortune. Visitors will not shut up about it, and neither will your colonists, which is rather the point.

ThingDef.label: pool filtration unit
ThingDef.description:
A sand filter, a circulation pump and a chlorinator in one housing. Stand it against any edge of a pool basin and it takes charge of every basin tile joined to that one, so a pool is whatever shape you painted rather than whatever shape somebody else decided on.

A bigger pool holds more water and costs more to circulate: both the fill and the power draw scale with the number of tiles. Off the plumbing, colonists carry the water in by hand from the nearest river, lake or marsh, a load at a time. With Dubs Bad Hygiene installed, pipe it in and it keeps itself topped up.

Cut the power, or lose the unit altogether, and the water stays but goes stale: murky within a few days, then foul, and colonists who swim in foul water can fall ill. A running unit clears it again.

ThingDef.label: hammock
ThingDef.description:
A slung sheet, deep enough to disappear into. A colonist gets in, stops having opinions about anything for half an hour, and gets out slightly less tired than they went in.

It hangs rather than stands: it needs a wall or a column directly beyond each end to be slung from, and cannot be built without both.

This is not a bed. Nobody is assigned to it, nobody sleeps the night in it, and no doctor will treat anyone in it. It is somewhere to do nothing, which the average colony has far too little of.

ThingDef.label: Thrumbo! arcade table
ThingDef.description:
The same sit-down cabinet running a different board. THRUMBO!: there is a colonist stranded at the top of a half-built scaffold and something enormous and extremely cross at the top of it throwing rocks down the girders at you. You climb. The rocks do not stop coming.

Nobody has ever reached the top. The high score is a matter of some dispute in the rec room.

Left alone it drops into attract mode and sits there running its title screen at nobody, which is somehow the most convincing thing about it.

Seats two - set a chair on either side. Quick reflexes help, and the ribbing that comes with them is half the point.

ThingDef.label: Infestation! arcade table
ThingDef.description:
The sit-down cabinet again, on its third board. INFESTATION!: rank on rank of insectoids - megaspiders at the back, spelopedes, megascarabs up front - sweep back and forth over a lone mini-turret dug in behind sandbags, spitting acid as they come. Pop one and it goes up in a splat of insect jelly. Something that looks a lot like a hive creeps across the top of the screen now and then.

Colonists who have lived through a real infestation play it with a particular grim focus. Everyone else just likes the noise it makes.

Left alone it runs its title screen, one enormous megaspider scuttling back and forth under the name.

Seats two - set a chair on either side.

ThingDef.label: cornhole board
ThingDef.description:
A sloped plank board with a hole near the high end, and a bag of dried corn for every player. Stand back, throw, argue about whether that one went in.

One colonist can practise at it alone. Two will take turns, each with their own colour of sack, which is the only version anybody actually enjoys. A third is told to wait.

The throwing line is a few tiles back - it is outlined while you place it, so leave the room clear. No power, no research, nothing but planks and cloth. Throwing trains shooting.

ThingDef.label: jigsaw table
ThingDef.description:
A broad low table with a jigsaw puzzle spread across it and the box lid propped at one end. The puzzle stays where it was left: anyone with a free evening pulls up a chair and adds a few pieces, and over several sittings the picture comes together.

When the last piece goes in, everyone who worked on it takes some quiet satisfaction from it. The finished puzzle can then be framed and hung on a wall, and the next one comes out of the box.

Needs chairs pulled up to its sides - as many colonists can work on it at once as there are chairs.

ThingDef.label: framed jigsaw (Thrumbo at Dawn)
ThingDef.description: A finished jigsaw puzzle, glued to a board and framed: a white thrumbo on a snowbound ridge, the sun coming up behind it. Every seam still shows if you look closely, which is rather the point.\n\nHangs on a wall like a lamp does and takes up no floor.

ThingDef.label: framed jigsaw (Muffalo Crossing)
ThingDef.description: A finished jigsaw puzzle, glued to a board and framed: a muffalo herd wading a tundra river in single file. Every seam still shows if you look closely, which is rather the point.\n\nHangs on a wall like a lamp does and takes up no floor.

ThingDef.label: framed jigsaw (Launch Day)
ThingDef.description: A finished jigsaw puzzle, glued to a board and framed: a ship climbing out of a sleeping colony on a column of fire. Every seam still shows if you look closely, which is rather the point.\n\nHangs on a wall like a lamp does and takes up no floor.

ThingDef.label: framed jigsaw (Boomalope Picnic)
ThingDef.description: A finished jigsaw puzzle, glued to a board and framed: a picnic in a spring meadow among grazing boomalopes, while something goes up in the distance and nobody notices. Every seam still shows if you look closely, which is rather the point.\n\nHangs on a wall like a lamp does and takes up no floor.

ThingDef.label: storyteller's stump
ThingDef.description:
A broad stump with a step cut into the front, for standing on. Put it beside a campfire, facing the side the listeners will sit.

When someone climbs up and starts telling a story, the rest of the colony drifts over to hear it - and while the story runs, its shapes rise out of the smoke: a thrumbo on a ridge, a raider with a rifle, a ship going up, a mechanoid coming down the hill. Everyone within earshot forms an opinion. A good talker, or a well-liked one, has the fire hanging on every word; a poor one is remembered for going on a bit.

Needs a lit fire within six tiles.

ThingDef.label: board game table
ThingDef.description:
A broad table and a cupboard of boxed games under it. Whoever sits down first picks one - never whatever was played last - and everyone who pulls up a chair after that is in:

- Colonists of the Rim: settle a ring of hexes, trade for what you are short of, argue about the robber.
- Raid!: the planet, carved up between four factions, one of which is mechanoids.
- Orbital Trader: buy up the trade routes round an orbit and charge everyone else for landing.
- Caravan Routes: claim the roads between towns before anyone else gets a caravan down them.
- Muffalo & Thrumbo: draughts, brown against white, crowned with horns.

Up to four players, one per chair pulled up to its sides. The board on the table shows which game is on.

ThingDef.label: seed pit board
ThingDef.description: A board with two rows of pits carved into it and a store at each end, and a bag of dried seeds to sow round them. Seed Pits is older than anyone can say: take up a pit, sow it round one seed at a time, capture what you land on. Two players, sitting on the ground either side of it if there is nothing better to sit on.

ThingDef.label: table tennis table
ThingDef.description: A long green table with a net strung across the middle and a pair of bats. Two colonists stand one at each end and knock a light ball back and forth over the net until somebody misses, which is usually quickly and always disputed.\n\nOne colonist alone can practise against the far end. Needs a clear tile at each end to stand on.

ThingDef.label: air hockey table
ThingDef.description: A table with a hissing surface full of tiny holes, a fan underneath, and a flat puck that floats on the air and goes wherever it is hit, very fast. Two colonists at the ends try to get it past each other's mallet into the slot, and bank it off the rails when they cannot.\n\nOne colonist can practise against the far end. Needs power, and a clear tile at each end to stand on.

ThingDef.label: lawn noughts and crosses
ThingDef.description: A three-by-three grid of rope pegged out on the ground, and a sack of bean bags in two colours. Noughts and crosses, except the marks have to be thrown into their squares from a line a few tiles back, which makes a simple game a great deal less simple.\n\nOne colonist can practise alone; two take turns. The rope lies flat, so it can be walked over.

ThingDef.label: giant four-in-a-row
ThingDef.description: An upright frame of seven columns taller than a child, and a crate of big coloured discs. Players take turns dropping a disc down a column; the first to line up four wins, and the loser pulls the release bar and lets the whole lot crash out onto the floor, which is the real reason anyone plays.\n\nTwo players stand in front of it. Face it the way the players should see it - from the sides it is only an edge.

ThingDef.label: tangle mat
ThingDef.description: A big white mat printed with rows of coloured spots, and a spinner card. Somebody spins; everyone has to get a hand or a foot onto the colour it lands on, without letting go of the spots they are already on. Up to three can play at once, which is two more than the mat was designed for.\n\nPeople fall over. That is the game.
